#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# seed-corpus-from-record.sh — build a review-recall fixture from a shipped
# sprint's round-1 state and its record-branch feedback (cycle-129 FR-2,
# SDD D-2.2, DEC-0154)
#
# Usage:
#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh <global-sprint> <record-ref> [--out <corpus>/pr-NN]
#                              [--base <rev>] [--head <rev>] [--fix <rev>]
#                              [--feedback a.md,b.md] [--dry-run]
#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --build-manifest pr-NN   # labels → hidden manifest (after curation)
#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <YYYY-MM-DD>"
#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --freeze                 # regenerate SHA256SUMS
#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --check                  # verify SHA256SUMS
#   common: [--repo <git dir>] [--corpus <evals/fixtures/review-prs>]
#
# Without --base/--head/--fix/--feedback/--out the sprint's row in
# <corpus>/record-pairs.tsv supplies them.
#
# Writes (seed):
#   <corpus>/pr-NN/{fixture.yaml, head.diff, PR.md, REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md,
#                   AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md, base/…, head/…}     (copied into the sandbox)
#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.tsv          HIDDEN (never copied into a sandbox): the labels,
#                                      first line `# approved-by: pending`
#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt  HIDDEN: every finding that did not become a label, and why
#   <corpus>/manifests/pr-NN.json      HIDDEN: the graded manifest (`approved: false` until --approve)
#   <corpus>/corpus.tsv                one `record` row per fixture (or a `#` gap comment)
#   evals/tasks/{review,audit}-recall/{review,audit}-pr-NN.yaml
#   <corpus>/SHA256SUMS                refreshed
#
# Scope: the fixture is the change base..head without the generated or state
# files (grimoires/, CHANGELOG.md, .claude/checksums.json, REPO-MAP.md, lock
# files, .beads/, .run/, evals/results/) and without binaries.
#
# Label rule: a feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit
# touches the file it cites (`git diff --name-only head..fix`) and that file
# is part of the fixture; label_source is review (engineer-feedback*,
# reviewer*), audit (auditor-sprint-feedback*) or bridgebuilder
# (bridgebuilder*, the "Fixed" table only). The anchor is a head-side line
# the fix changed near the cited line or inside the cited symbol; a finding
# that cites only a file is anchored on that file's fix hunks when there are
# at most four, else dropped. `fix` rows cover every hunk fix_commit changed
# in a fixture file (source fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>); the grader uses them
# only for refuted share. Titles are control-stripped, capped at 160 chars,
# and a title matching a secret pattern drops its finding; every written
# file passes evals/graders/no-secrets.sh or the seed fails.
#
# Exit: 0 ok, 1 refused / spec error / secret found / check failed, 2 usage
# Tested by evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

exec python3 -I - "$REPO_ROOT" "$@" <<'PY'
import argparse, csv, hashlib, io, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile

HARNESS_ROOT = sys.argv[1]
argv = sys.argv[2:]

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="seed-corpus-from-record.sh", add_help=True)
ap.add_argument("sprint", nargs="?")
ap.add_argument("record_ref", nargs="?")
ap.add_argument("--out"); ap.add_argument("--base"); ap.add_argument("--head"); ap.add_argument("--fix")
ap.add_argument("--feedback"); ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--build-manifest", metavar="FIXTURE"); ap.add_argument("--approve", metavar="FIXTURE")
ap.add_argument("--by"); ap.add_argument("--freeze", action="store_true"); ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--repo", default=HARNESS_ROOT)
ap.add_argument("--corpus", default=os.path.join(HARNESS_ROOT, "evals", "fixtures", "review-prs"))
ap.add_argument("--tasks-dir", default=os.path.join(HARNESS_ROOT, "evals", "tasks"))
try:
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
except SystemExit as e:
    sys.exit(2 if e.code else 0)

REPO, CORPUS = os.path.abspath(args.repo), os.path.abspath(args.corpus)
NO_SECRETS = os.path.join(HARNESS_ROOT, "evals", "graders", "no-secrets.sh")
LABELS_DIR = os.path.join(CORPUS, "labels")
MANIFESTS_DIR = os.path.join(CORPUS, "manifests")
FX_RX = re.compile(r"^pr-[0-9]{2}$")
HEADER = ["defect_id", "severity", "category", "file", "must_match", "label_source", "source"]

def fail(msg, code=1):
    print(f"seed-corpus: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(code)

def git(*a, binary=False, check=True):
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, *a], capture_output=True, text=not binary)
    if check and p.returncode != 0:
        fail(f"git {' '.join(a[:3])} failed: {(p.stderr if not binary else p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace')).strip()[:300]}")
    return p.stdout

def rev(r):
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{r}^{{commit}}"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        fail(f"missing commit: {r}")
    return p.stdout.strip()

def show(r, path):
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "show", f"{r}:{path}"], capture_output=True)
    return p.stdout if p.returncode == 0 else None

CTRL = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f  ]")
def clean(s, cap=160):
    s = CTRL.sub(" ", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
    return s if len(s) <= cap else s[: cap - 1].rstrip() + "…"

SECRET_RX = [re.compile(p) for p in (
    r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}", r"sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}", r"ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}", r"gho_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}",
    r"glpat-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}", r"xox[bpors]-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+", r"sk-ant-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}",
    r"password\s*[:=]\s*[\"'][^\"']{8,}", r"secret\s*[:=]\s*[\"'][^\"']{8,}")]
def has_secret(s):
    return any(r.search(s) for r in SECRET_RX)

REDACTED = [0]
def redact(b, count=True):
    """Secret-shaped strings in verbatim copies of tracked files (fake test keys)
    become a fixed marker, identically in base/, head/ and head.diff; line
    numbers never move. Counted in the dropped report."""
    if b is None:
        return None
    t = b.decode("utf-8", "replace") if isinstance(b, bytes) else b
    for r in SECRET_RX:
        t, n = r.subn("REDACTED-TEST-SECRET", t)
        REDACTED[0] += n if count else 0
    return t.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(b, bytes) else t

def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(open(path, "rb").read()).hexdigest()

def freeze():
    entries = []
    for root, _d, files in os.walk(CORPUS):
        for f in files:
            rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), CORPUS)
            if rel != "SHA256SUMS":
                entries.append(rel)
    lines = [f"{sha(os.path.join(CORPUS, rel))}  {rel}" for rel in sorted(entries)]
    open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), "w").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    return len(lines)

def check():
    bad, n = [], 0
    for line in open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), encoding="utf-8"):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        n += 1
        d, rel = line.rstrip("\n").split("  ", 1)
        p = os.path.join(CORPUS, rel)
        if not os.path.isfile(p) or sha(p) != d:
            bad.append(rel)
    listed = {l.rstrip("\n").split("  ", 1)[1] for l in open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()}
    for root, _d, files in os.walk(CORPUS):
        for f in files:
            rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), CORPUS)
            if rel != "SHA256SUMS" and rel not in listed:
                bad.append(rel + " (not listed)")
    if bad:
        fail("SHA256SUMS mismatch: " + ", ".join(bad[:20]))
    print(f"corpus OK: {n} files match SHA256SUMS")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- labels I/O
def read_labels(fx):
    path = os.path.join(LABELS_DIR, f"{fx}.tsv")
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        fail(f"labels not found: {path}")
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()
    if not text or not re.match(r"^# approved-by: \S", text[0]):
        fail(f"{path}: the first line must be '# approved-by: <who> <date>' (or 'pending')")
    approved_by = text[0][len("# approved-by: "):].strip()
    body = [l for l in text[1:] if l and not l.startswith("#")]
    if not body or body[0].split("\t") != HEADER:
        fail(f"{path}: header must be: " + "\t".join(HEADER))
    rows = []
    for i, l in enumerate(body[1:], 2):
        cells = l.split("\t")
        if len(cells) != len(HEADER):
            fail(f"{path}: row {i} has {len(cells)} columns, want {len(HEADER)}")
        rows.append(dict(zip(HEADER, cells)))
    return approved_by, rows, text

def unique_line(lines, needle):
    hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines, 1) if needle in l]
    return hits[0] if len(hits) == 1 else None

def build_manifest(fx):
    approved_by, rows, _ = read_labels(fx)
    fyaml = os.path.join(CORPUS, fx, "fixture.yaml")
    meta = {}
    for l in open(fyaml, encoding="utf-8"):
        m = re.match(r"^(sprint|head_commit|fix_commit|record_ref):\s*\"?([^\"\n]*)\"?$", l)
        if m:
            meta[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
    defects, regions, errors, order = {}, [], [], []
    for r in rows:
        if r["label_source"] not in ("review", "audit", "bridgebuilder", "fix"):
            errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: label_source {r['label_source']!r}"); continue
        hp = os.path.join(CORPUS, fx, "head", r["file"])
        if not os.path.isfile(hp):
            errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: head/{r['file']} missing"); continue
        lines = open(hp, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read().splitlines()
        if r["label_source"] == "fix":
            m = re.match(r"^fix/[0-9a-f]+:(\d+)-(\d+)$", r["source"])
            if not m:
                errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: fix source must be fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>"); continue
            regions.append({"id": r["defect_id"], "file": r["file"], "start": int(m.group(1)), "end": int(m.group(2)),
                            "source": r["source"]})
            continue
        at = unique_line(lines, r["must_match"])
        if at is None:
            errors.append(f"{r['defect_id']}: must_match {r['must_match']!r} is not on exactly one line of head/{r['file']}"); continue
        d = defects.get(r["defect_id"])
        if d is None:
            order.append(r["defect_id"])
            defects[r["defect_id"]] = {"id": r["defect_id"], "file": r["file"], "anchor_line": at, "anchors": [at],

diff --git a/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md b/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
index a6e116bf..b3a69cf6 100644
--- a/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+++ b/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
@@ -50,11 +50,15 @@ ## Language
 **Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.
 _Aliases_: jack out
 
+**Judgment**: The task kind for work that needs reading and a decision; it ships as prose or a reviewed artifact, and its sprint task line ends with kind: judgment.
+
 **Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
 _Avoid_: converged
 
 **Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
 
+**Kind counts**: The release-notes line that counts a cycle's sprint tasks by kind (mechanical, judgment and operator), read from the tagged task lines of its sprint plan.
+
 **Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
 _Aliases_: KF
 
@@ -62,6 +66,10 @@ ## Language
 
 **Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
 
+**Mechanical**: The task kind for work a script could do reliably; it ships as code with tests, and a review flags a mechanical task delivered as prose the model re-executes.
+
+**Operator**: The human who owns the project and its decisions; as a task kind, work that belongs to that human, which a review flags when it was completed unattended without a decision:unblock ticket or a DEC row.
+
 **Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
 
 **Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.
@@ -78,4 +86,6 @@ ## Language
 
 **Voice**: The party a decision or finding is attributed to: the operator, the agent, Flatline or dissent.
 
+**Volume ratio**: The release-notes line that sets a cycle's script lines changed against its prose bytes changed and its model calls; the model-call count is local to the host that ran the cycle.
+
 **Zone**: One of the three permission regions of a repository: the System zone holds the framework and is never edited by hand, the State zone is read and written freely, and the App zone needs confirmation before a write.

 ## All Hook Registrations
 
-See `.claude/hooks/settings.hooks.json` for the complete hook configuration.
+Generated from `.claude/settings.json` (the registrations Claude Code runs) and `.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml` (status, knob, purpose) by `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table`; CI fails on drift (`--check`). The full guard register, with fence pattern ids, validator rules, gates and origins, is `grimoires/loa/guards.md`.
 
-| Event | Matcher | Script | Purpose |
-|-------|---------|--------|---------|
-| PreCompact | (all) | `pre-compact-marker.sh` | Save state before compaction |
-| UserPromptSubmit | (all) | `post-compact-reminder.sh` | Inject recovery after compaction |
-| UserPromptSubmit | (all) | `post-session-limit-reminder.sh` | Inject resume reminder after a session cap resets |
-| SessionStart | (all) | `hook-guard.sh session-start/loa-run-state-surface.sh` | One `Run: <state> (<age>) → <command>` line when a run is HALTED/INTERRUPTED or RUNNING idle 12h+, plus a session-limit-reset line; silent otherwise (cycle-125 FR-3; also feeds `/loa` and `workflow-state.sh`) |
-| SessionStart | (all) | `hook-guard.sh session-start/loa-context-class.sh` | Writes `.run/context-class` — `long` by default, `standard` under `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard` or a ≤ 200K session model — the class the skills' context-discipline thresholds follow (`tool-result-clearing.md`); `/loa` shows it; a re-fire on clear/compact/resume with no model keeps a `model`/`env` record; silent, never blocks |
-| SessionStart | (all) | `hook-guard.sh session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh` | Default off (`decisions.surface_at_session_start`): up to ten `proposed`/`open` decision rows inside the L6 data fence, plus a stale unattended-marker notice; see [Decision surfaces](#decision-surfaces-cycle-128) |
-| PreToolUse | Bash | `safety/block-destructive-bash.sh` | Block destructive commands |
-| PreToolUse | Bash | `safety/team-role-guard.sh` | Enforce lead-only ops in Agent Teams |
-| PreToolUse | Write | `safety/team-role-guard-write.sh` | Block teammate writes to System Zone, state files, and append-only files |
-| PreToolUse | Edit | `safety/team-role-guard-write.sh` | Block teammate edits to System Zone, state files, and append-only files |
-| PreToolUse | Skill | `safety/team-skill-guard.sh` | Block lead-only skill invocations for teammates |
-| PreToolUse | Write/Edit/MultiEdit | `safety/notes-size-guard.sh` | Refuse a write that would grow `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md` at/over 200 KiB (shrinking edits and `notes-guard.sh rotate` pass) |
-| PostToolUse | Bash | `audit/mutation-logger.sh` | Log mutating commands |
-| PostToolUse | Write | `audit/write-mutation-logger.sh` | Log Write tool file modifications |
-| PostToolUse | Edit | `audit/write-mutation-logger.sh` | Log Edit tool file modifications |
-| Stop | (all) | `safety/run-mode-stop-guard.sh` | Guard against premature exit |
-| PreToolUse | Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit | `hook-guard.sh compliance/implement-gate.sh` | ADVISORY: `ask` on an App Zone write outside an active implementation run, on a write to the gate's own trust inputs, and whenever the write cannot be evaluated; never blocks (§implement-gate.sh) |
-| Stop (opt-in, UNREGISTERED by default) | (all) | `safety/stop-input-probe.sh` | DIAGNOSTIC: gated by `LOA_STOP_INPUT_PROBE=1`; dumps raw Stop input to `.run/stop-input-probe.jsonl` for one cap-hitting session — never in `settings.hooks.json` |

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
     4	# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
     5	#
     6	#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
     7	#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
     8	#
     9	# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
    10	#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
    11	#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
    12	#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
    13	#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
    14	#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
    15	#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
    16	#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
    17	#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
    18	#                  binary files skipped)
    19	#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
    20	#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
    21	#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
    22	#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
    23	#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
    24	#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
    25	#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
    26	#
    27	# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
    28	# default to paths under its top level.
    29	#
    30	# Usage:
    31	#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
    32	#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
    33	#
    34	#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    35	#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
    36	#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
    37	#
    38	# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
    39	# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
    46	
    47	SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    48	FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"
    49	
    50	FROM=""
    51	TO=""
    52	PLAN=""
    53	MODELINV=""
    54	JSON=0
    55	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    56	  case "$1" in
    57	    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
    58	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    59	      case "$1" in
    60	        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
    61	        --to) TO="$2" ;;
    62	        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
    63	        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
    64	      esac
    65	      shift 2 ;;
    66	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    67	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    68	    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    69	  esac
    70	done
    71	
    72	[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    73	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
    74	TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
    75	[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    76	[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.1)
+#
+# execute-agent.sh applies a control arm's toggles to the sandbox copy only.
+# Every assertion here reads the sandbox as the EXECUTOR saw it: the CLI stub
+# snapshots CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .loa.config.yaml and the appended system
+# prompt at the moment it starts (STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR), after every
+# materialisation step. The arm ids and toggles come from the real suite
+# files; the prompt tree is a synthetic fixture so later prose edits to the
+# live kernel cannot change what this test proves.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  EXEC="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh"
+  REVIEW_SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/review-recall.yaml"
+  AUDIT_SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/audit-recall.yaml"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/at.XXXXXX")"
+  WS="$T/ws"; SNAP="$T/snap"
+  mkdir -p "$WS"
+  ( cd "$WS" && git init -q && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q --allow-empty -m init )
+  export EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub.sh"
+  export EVAL_MODEL="claude-fable-5-1"
+  export STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR="$SNAP"
+  unset LOA_EVAL_ARM LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT EVAL_EFFORT
+
+  # --- synthetic prompt tree (the shape of 864069f2) ---
+  PT="$T/tree"
+  mkdir -p "$PT/.claude/loa" "$PT/.claude/rules" "$PT/.claude/data" \
+    "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code" "$PT/.claude/skills/auditing-security"
+  printf '%s\n' "# Loa Framework Instructions" "" "## Three-Zone Model" "" "zones" "" \
+    "## Karpathy Principles" "" "Every code-touching turn." "" "1. **Think before coding** — state assumptions." "" \
+    "## Process Compliance" "" "rules" > "$PT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  echo "# Git Stash Safety" > "$PT/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md"
+  echo "# Skill Frontmatter Invariants" > "$PT/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md"
+  printf '%s\n' "---" "paths:" '  - "grimoires/**"' "---" "# zone state" > "$PT/.claude/rules/zone-state.md"
+  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: reviewing-code" "---" "# Review" "Review the diff." > "$PT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
+  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: auditing-security" "---" "# Audit" "" "### Coverage" "" \
+    "Report every finding you actually observe." "" \
+    "Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under" \
+    "\`excluded\`, either confirm it or tally it as a finding of your own." "" \
+    "## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally" "" "Count every finding." > "$PT/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
+  printf '%s\n' "flatline_protocol:" "  code_review:" "    enabled: true" "  security_audit:" "    enabled: true" > "$PT/.loa.config.yaml"
+  ( cd "$PT" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m tree )
+  export EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$PT"
+
+  for s in reviewing-code auditing-security; do
+    cat > "$T/task-$s.yaml" <<YAML
+id: at-$s
+schema_version: 1
+skill: $s
+category: skill-quality
+fixture: hello-world-ts
+description: "arm toggle task"
+prompt: "Read the instructions and carry them out."
+agent:
+  skill: $s
+  artifacts: [review.md]
+graders:
+  - type: code
+    script: file-exists.sh
+    args: ["review.md"]
+YAML
+  done
+}
+
+teardown() {
+  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
+  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+run_arm() {  # run_arm <arm> <suite-file> <skill>
+  LOA_EVAL_ARM="$1" LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE="$2" run "$EXEC" --task-yaml "$T/task-$3.yaml" --workspace "$WS"
+}
+
+@test "AT-1 both suites declare the canonical arm ids and the pre-registered threshold block" {
+  [ "$(yq -r '[.ab.arms[].id] | join(",")' "$REVIEW_SUITE")" = "baseline,no_companion,no_karpathy,no_rule_files" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '[.ab.arms[].id] | join(",")' "$AUDIT_SUITE")" = "baseline,no_audit_delta" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.ab.arms[] | select(.id=="no_companion") | .informational' "$REVIEW_SUITE")" = "true" ]
+  yq -r '.ab.arms[] | select(.id=="no_karpathy") | .description' "$REVIEW_SUITE" | grep -q 'kernel block only'
+  for s in "$REVIEW_SUITE" "$AUDIT_SUITE"; do
+    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.trials_required' "$s")" = "3" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.coverage_required' "$s")" = "full" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.mean_recall_max_drop' "$s")" = "0.10" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.min_trial_recall_max_drop' "$s")" = "0.15" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.refuted_share_max_rise' "$s")" = "0.10" ]
+    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.threshold.bootstrap | [.method, .level, .resample, .iterations] | join(",")' "$s")" = "percentile,0.90,fixtures,2000" ]
+    # the existing freshness keys are untouched
+    [ "$(yq -r '.ab.corpus_manifest' "$s")" = "evals/fixtures/review-prs/SHA256SUMS" ]
+  done
+}

+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$SNAP/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  [ -f "$SNAP/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md" ]
+  [ -f "$SNAP/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md" ]
+  [ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$SNAP/.loa.config.yaml")" = "null" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.arm' "$WS/.eval/executor.json")" = "baseline" ]
+  [ "$(jq -c '.arm_toggles' "$WS/.eval/executor.json")" = "{}" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.source_commit' "$WS/.eval/executor.json")" = "$(git -C "$PT" rev-parse HEAD)" ]
+}
+
+@test "AT-3 audit baseline: the delta paragraph is in the sandbox SKILL.md and the system prompt" {
+  run_arm baseline "$AUDIT_SUITE" auditing-security
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -q "Confirm the review's demotions independently" "$SNAP/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
+  grep -q "Confirm the review's demotions independently" "$SNAP/system-prompt.md"
+}
+
+@test "AT-4 no_rule_files: the two rule files are absent at executor start; other rules stay; the source tree is untouched" {
+  run_arm no_rule_files "$REVIEW_SUITE" reviewing-code
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ ! -e "$SNAP/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md" ]
+  [ ! -e "$SNAP/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md" ]
+  [ -f "$SNAP/.claude/rules/zone-state.md" ]

@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# Path-scoped rule files (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-3.1, DEC-0129): stash-safety.md and
+# skill-invariants.md carry `paths:` frontmatter, the frontmatter parses, and every glob
+# matches at least one tracked file of the kind the rule is about (git pathspec glob
+# semantics: `**` spans directories, `*` stays inside one).
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    RULES="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/rules"
+    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"
+}
+
+# The YAML between the first two '---' lines (empty when the file has none).
+frontmatter() { awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" { exit } /^---$/ { if (n++) exit; next } n' "$1"; }
+globs() { frontmatter "$1" | yq eval '.paths[]' -; }
+tracked() { git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" ls-files -- ":(glob)$1"; }
+
+@test "RP-1 both rule files open with frontmatter that parses and lists string globs under paths:" {
+    local f n
+    for f in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
+        [ "$(head -1 "$RULES/$f")" = "---" ] || { echo "$f has no frontmatter"; return 1; }
+        frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.' - >/dev/null || { echo "$f frontmatter does not parse"; return 1; }
+        [ "$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.paths | type' -)" = "!!seq" ]
+        n="$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.paths | length' -)"
+        [ "$n" -ge 1 ]
+        [ "$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '[.paths[] | select(type != "!!str")] | length' -)" -eq 0 ]
+    done
+}
+
+@test "RP-2 the globs are the ones the SDD names" {
+    [ "$(globs "$RULES/stash-safety.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = '**/*.sh **/*.bats .claude/scripts/** .claude/hooks/** ' ]
+    [ "$(globs "$RULES/skill-invariants.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = '.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md .claude/agents/** .claude/data/agent-types.yaml .claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh ' ]
+}
+
+@test "RP-3 every stash-safety glob matches a tracked shell source" {
+    local g hits
+    while IFS= read -r g; do
+        hits="$(tracked "$g" | grep -E '\.(sh|bats)$' | head -1)"
+        [ -n "$hits" ] || { echo "glob '$g' matches no tracked .sh/.bats file"; return 1; }
+    done < <(globs "$RULES/stash-safety.md")
+}
+
+@test "RP-4 every skill-invariants glob matches a tracked skill, agent definition or capability file" {
+    local g hits
+    while IFS= read -r g; do
+        hits="$(tracked "$g" | grep -E '(^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$|^\.claude/agents/[^/]+\.md$|^\.claude/data/agent-types\.yaml$|^\.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities\.sh$)' | head -1)"
+        [ -n "$hits" ] || { echo "glob '$g' matches no tracked file of the intended kind"; return 1; }
+    done < <(globs "$RULES/skill-invariants.md")
+}
+
+@test "RP-5 path-scoping removed no rule text: the body after the frontmatter keeps its heading and sections" {
+    local body
+    body="$(awk '/^---$/ && c < 2 { c++; next } c >= 2' "$RULES/stash-safety.md")"
+    [[ "$body" == *"# Git Stash Safety"* && "$body" == *"## Judgment rules the fence cannot express"* ]]
+    body="$(awk '/^---$/ && c < 2 { c++; next } c >= 2' "$RULES/skill-invariants.md")"
+    [[ "$body" == *"# Skill Frontmatter Invariants"* && "$body" == *"## The invariant"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RP-6 the rule-lifecycle validator accepts both files (origin, version, enacted_by)" {
+    run "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/validate-rule-lifecycle.sh" --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/guard-yield.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1 AC-1.2 … AC-1.4,
     5	# SDD D-1.3, D-1.4)
     6	# guard-yield.sh over a fixture audit log and a rotated segment, at a fixed
     7	# --now: replay exclusion (flag, cwd, burst) counted in the header, the
     8	# likely-false-positive heuristic (heredoc, outside-repo cwd, prose class without
     9	# a destructive verb at statement start), day-granular last_real_catch, the
    10	# --check drift gate (0 after generation, 1 after an origin edit, 0 after a
    11	# yield-only change), the --json shape, and no command text or cwd in any output.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	NOW="2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
    15	
    16	setup() {
    17	  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
    18	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    19	  GY="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh"
    20	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gyield.XXXXXX")"
    21	  T="$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)"
    22	  mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/scratch"
    23	  # A temp prefix the fixture controls (the script's own mktemp also uses it).
    24	  export TMPDIR="$T"
    25	  cp "$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml" "$T/origins.yaml"
    26	  cp "$ROOT/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md" "$T/hooks-reference.md"
    27	  A="$T/audit.jsonl"
    28	  row() {  # ts pattern cwd command [extra-json]
    29	    jq -cn --arg ts "$1" --arg p "$2" --arg cwd "$3" --arg c "$4" --argjson x "${5:-{\}}" \
    30	      '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", command: $c, exit_code: 2, cwd: $cwd, model: "claude-test-model", hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: $p, matched: "m"} + $x'
    31	  }
    32	  {
    33	    # live, inside the repo
    34	    row "2026-10-12T08:00:00Z" "FR-SZ2-REDIR" "$ROOT" "cat > .claude/x.md <<'EOF'"            # heredoc → likely FP
    35	    row "2026-10-12T09:00:00Z" "P2" "/srv/elsewhere/scratch" "git push --force origin topic"    # outside repo → likely FP
    36	    row "2026-10-12T10:00:00Z" "SP-1" "$ROOT" "br comments add bd-1 'note about spike/x merge'" # prose class, no verb → likely FP
    37	    row "2026-10-13T23:59:00Z" "FR-2-AMBIGUOUS" "$ROOT" "cd sub && rm -rf ./.cache"             # prose class WITH verb → real
    38	    # replays
    39	    row "2026-10-11T08:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~1" '{"replay": true}'        # flag
    40	    row "2026-10-11T09:00:00Z" "P3" "$T/scratch" "git reset --hard HEAD~2"                       # cwd under TMPDIR
    41	    row "2026-10-11T10:00:00Z" "P3" "/home/u/bats-run-42/repo" "git reset --hard HEAD~3"        # cwd /bats-run-
    42	    for s in 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09; do                                                  # burst: 10 in one minute
    43	      row "2026-10-09T10:00:${s}Z" "P2" "$ROOT" "git push --force origin main"
    44	    done
    45	    # outside the window
    46	    row "2026-08-01T08:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~9"
    47	    # implement-gate telemetry and ask
    48	    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:00:00Z", hook: "implement-gate", action: "telemetry", cwd: "x"}'
    49	    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:05:00Z", hook: "implement-gate", action: "ask", cwd: "x"}'
    50	    # a non-block row and an unparseable line
    51	    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:10:00Z", tool: "Bash", command: "ls", cwd: "x"}'
    52	    printf 'this is not json\n'
    53	  } > "$A"
    54	  # the rotated segment holds the one real P3 catch
    55	  row "2026-10-10T09:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~3" > "$A.1"
    56	  ARGS=(--now "$NOW" --audit-log "$A" --origins "$T/origins.yaml" --out "$T/guards.md" --yield-dir "$T/run" --hooks-ref "$T/hooks-reference.md")
    57	}
    58	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    59	
    60	g() { jq -c --arg id "$1" '.guards[] | select(.id == $id) | [.blocks_30d, .likely_fp_30d, .telemetry_30d, .last_real_catch]' "$T/run/guard-yield.json"; }
    61	
    62	@test "GY-1 replay rows are excluded by flag, cwd and burst and counted in the header; the window and bad rows are honoured" {
    63	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
    64	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output" >&2; false; }
    65	  J="$T/run/guard-yield.json"
    66	  [ "$(jq '.audit_segments' "$J")" = "2" ]
    67	  [ "$(jq '.audit_rows_considered' "$J")" = "20" ]
    68	  [ "$(jq '.replay_rows_excluded' "$J")" = "13" ]
    69	  [ "$(jq -c '.replay_rows_by_rule' "$J")" = '{"flag":1,"cwd":2,"burst":10}' ]
    70	  [ "$(jq '.audit_rows_unparseable' "$J")" = "1" ]
    71	  [ "$(jq -c '.totals | [.blocks_30d, .real_blocks_30d, .likely_fp_30d, .telemetry_30d]' "$J")" = '[5,2,3,2]' ]
    72	  [ "$(jq -r '.scope' "$J")" = "host" ]
    73	  [ "$(jq -r '.window_days' "$J")" = "30" ]
    74	}
    75	
    76	@test "GY-2 the rotated segment is read: its real P3 catch is counted and is the guard's last_real_catch" {
    77	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
    78	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    79	  [ "$(g fence:P3)" = '[1,0,0,"2026-10-10"]' ]
    80	}
    81	
    82	@test "GY-3 heredoc, scratch-path and prose-class blocks classify as likely false positives; a prose class with a destructive verb is real" {
    83	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
    84	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    85	  [ "$(g fence:FR-SZ2-REDIR)" = '[1,1,0,"none in window"]' ]
    86	  [ "$(g fence:P2)" = '[1,1,0,"none in window"]' ]
    87	  [ "$(g fence:SP-1)" = '[1,1,0,"none in window"]' ]
    88	  [ "$(g fence:FR-2-AMBIGUOUS)" = '[1,0,0,"2026-10-13"]' ]
    89	  [ "$(g hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh)" = '[5,3,0,"2026-10-13"]' ]
    90	}
    91	
    92	@test "GY-4 last_real_catch and generated_at are day-granular; telemetry counts implement-gate rows; non-writers show n/a" {
    93	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
    94	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    95	  J="$T/run/guard-yield.json"
    96	  [ "$(jq -r '.generated_at' "$J")" = "2026-10-14" ]
    97	  [ -z "$(jq -r '.guards[].last_real_catch' "$J" | grep -vE '^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}|none in window|n/a)$' || true)" ]
    98	  [ "$(g gate:implement-gate)" = '[0,0,2,"none in window"]' ]
    99	  [ "$(g hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh)" = '[0,0,2,"none in window"]' ]
   100	  [ "$(g hook:safety/zone-write-guard.sh)" = '[null,null,null,"n/a"]' ]
   101	  grep -qE '^\| hook:safety/zone-write-guard.sh \|.*\| n/a \| n/a \| n/a \| n/a \|$' "$T/run/guard-yield.md"
   102	}
   103	
   104	@test "GY-5 no command text, cwd, hostname or model name reaches guards.md, the yield files or the hooks table" {
   105	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --hooks-table
   106	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   107	  # the hooks reference documents fence commands in its own prose; only the generated block is checked
   108	  awk '/^<!-- guard-register:begin -->$/,/^<!-- guard-register:end -->$/' "$T/hooks-reference.md" > "$T/hooks-block.md"
   109	  [ -s "$T/hooks-block.md" ]
   110	  for f in "$T/guards.md" "$T/run/guard-yield.md" "$T/run/guard-yield.json" "$T/hooks-block.md"; do
   111	    for needle in "reset --hard" "push --force" "rm -rf" "spike/x merge" "<<'EOF'" "/srv/elsewhere" "bats-run-42" "$T" "claude-test-model" "$(hostname)"; do
   112	      if grep -qF -- "$needle" "$f"; then echo "$f leaks '$needle'" >&2; false; fi
   113	    done
   114	  done
   115	}
   116	
   117	@test "GY-6 guards.md is structural: header counts, one table per kind, no timestamp, and identical whatever the audit log holds" {
   118	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
   119	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   120	  n="$(yq '.guards | length' "$T/origins.yaml")"
   121	  grep -qx -- "- guards: $n" "$T/guards.md"
   122	  grep -qx -- "- guards_without_origin: 0" "$T/guards.md"
   123	  grep -qx -- "- dormant: 3" "$T/guards.md"
   124	  for k in hook fence validator gate policy; do grep -qE "^## $k \([0-9]+\)$" "$T/guards.md"; done
   125	  [ "$(grep -cE '^\| (hook|fence|validator|gate|policy):' "$T/guards.md")" -eq "$n" ]
   126	  ! grep -qE '20[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T|generated_at' "$T/guards.md"
   127	  cp "$T/guards.md" "$T/guards.first"
   128	  : > "$A"; rm -f "$A.1"
   129	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
   130	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   131	  cmp "$T/guards.first" "$T/guards.md"
   132	}
   133	
   134	@test "GY-7 --check exits 0 after generation, 1 after an origin edit (with the regenerate hint), 0 after a yield-only change" {
   135	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --hooks-table
   136	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   137	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --check
   138	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   139	  # yield-only change: more audit rows, regenerate the yield; the structure is untouched
   140	  jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-14T08:00:00Z", hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: "P4", cwd: "/x", command: "git clean -fd"}' >> "$A"
   141	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
   142	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   143	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --check
   144	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   145	  # origin edit
   146	  yq -i '(.guards[] | select(.id == "fence:P3") | .origin.ref) = "cycle-011 edited"' "$T/origins.yaml"
   147	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --check
   148	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   149	  [[ "$output" == *"drift"*"guards.md"* ]]
   150	  [[ "$output" == *"regenerate: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table"* ]]
   151	  # a purpose edit drifts the hooks table too
   152	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
   153	  yq -i '(.guards[] | select(.id == "hook:safety/notes-size-guard.sh") | .note) = "edited purpose"' "$T/origins.yaml"
   154	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --check
   155	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   156	  [[ "$output" == *"guard-register table"* ]]
   157	}
   158	
   159	@test "GY-8 --hooks-table writes one row per registration between the markers, including the six hooks the hand table omitted" {
   160	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --hooks-table
   161	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   162	  block="$(awk '/^<!-- guard-register:begin -->$/,/^<!-- guard-register:end -->$/' "$T/hooks-reference.md")"
   163	  regs="$(jq '[.hooks | to_entries[] | .value[] | .hooks[]] | length' "$ROOT/.claude/settings.json")"
   164	  [ "$(grep -E '^\| [A-Za-z]+ \|' <<<"$block" | grep -cv '^| Event |')" -eq "$regs" ]
   165	  for s in safety/zone-write-guard.sh safety/spiral-dispatch-guard.sh safety/spiral-skill-sentinel.sh safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh scripts/upgrade-health-check.sh scripts/permission-audit.sh; do
   166	    grep -qF "$s" <<<"$block" || { echo "hooks table misses $s" >&2; false; }
   167	  done
   168	  grep -qE '^\| PreToolUse \| Bash \| `hook-guard.sh safety/team-role-guard.sh` \| dormant \| LOA_TEAM_MEMBER \|' <<<"$block"
   169	  grep -qE '^\| PreToolUse \| Write\\\|Edit\\\|MultiEdit\\\|NotebookEdit \|' <<<"$block"
   170	}
   171	
   172	@test "GY-9 --json prints the yield object (header, totals and one row per guard)" {
   173	  run --separate-stderr bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --json
   174	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   175	  n="$(yq '.guards | length' "$T/origins.yaml")"
   176	  jq -e --argjson n "$n" '
   177	    (keys | contains(["schema_version","generated_at","window_days","scope","audit_segments","audit_rows_considered","replay_rows_excluded","replay_rows_by_rule","heuristic","totals","guards"]))
   178	    and (.guards | length) == $n
   179	    and all(.guards[]; has("id") and has("class") and has("status") and has("origin") and has("knob") and has("floor") and has("registrations") and has("blocks_30d") and has("likely_fp_30d") and has("telemetry_30d") and has("last_real_catch"))
   180	    and (.totals | has("real_blocks_30d") and has("likely_fp_30d"))' <<<"$output" >/dev/null
   181	}
   182	
   183	@test "GY-10 a missing audit log is a WARN and an empty yield (exit 0); a missing origin row is exit 5" {
   184	  run bash "$GY" --now "$NOW" --audit-log "$T/none.jsonl" --origins "$T/origins.yaml" --out "$T/guards.md" --yield-dir "$T/run"
   185	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   186	  [[ "$output" == *"WARN: no audit log"* ]]
   187	  [ "$(jq '.audit_rows_considered + .totals.blocks_30d' "$T/run/guard-yield.json")" = "0" ]
   188	  yq -i 'del(.guards[] | select(.id == "hook:safety/notes-size-guard.sh"))' "$T/origins.yaml"
   189	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
   190	  [ "$status" -eq 5 ]
   191	  [[ "$output" == *"guard hook:safety/notes-size-guard.sh has no origin row"* ]]
   192	}
   193	
   194	@test "GY-11 a 10,000-row audit log is joined in under 10 seconds" {
   195	  jq -cn --arg r "$ROOT" 'range(10000) | {ts: "2026-10-12T08:\(. % 60 | tostring | if length == 1 then "0" + . else . end):00Z", hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: (if . % 2 == 0 then "block" else "allow-marker" end), pattern_id: "P2", cwd: $r, command: "git push --force origin b\(.)"}' > "$A"
   196	  rm -f "$A.1"
   197	  start=$(date +%s)
   198	  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
   199	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   200	  [ $(( $(date +%s) - start )) -lt 10 ]
   201	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1 AC-1.1, SDD D-1.6)
     5	# The origin map .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml covers every guard the
     6	# repository enumerates: every hook script registered in .claude/settings.json,
     7	# every fence pattern id in block-destructive-bash.sh, every validator rule
     8	# marker in validate-artifact.sh, the fixed gate list and the floor policies.
     9	# The enumeration here is independent of guard-yield.sh (its own jq/grep), so a
    10	# bug in the script cannot hide a gap. Fixture copies prove the failure modes.
    11	# =============================================================================
    12	
    13	# The sha256 of .claude/data/floor.yaml. An edit to the floor fails this suite
    14	# until the pin is updated deliberately, in the same change, with a reviewer:
    15	#   bash -c 'source .claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh; sha256_portable .claude/data/floor.yaml'
    16	FLOOR_SHA256="bd1f22dce9b6f18a0fda36d5a65dacd8103075c66c8c649b21de04fffcc92587"
    17	
    18	setup() {
    19	  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
    20	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    21	  GY="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh"
    22	  MAP="$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml"
    23	  FLOOR="$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
    24	  SETTINGS="$ROOT/.claude/settings.json"
    25	  FENCE="$ROOT/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
    26	  VALIDATOR="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
    27	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gorig.XXXXXX")"
    28	  # Fixture outputs never touch the tracked register or the live .run.
    29	  OUTARGS=(--out "$T/guards.md" --yield-dir "$T/run" --audit-log "$T/no-audit.jsonl")
    30	}
    31	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    32	
    33	# ids of every registered hook script, derived independently of guard-yield.sh
    34	enumerated_hook_ids() {
    35	  jq -r '.hooks | to_entries[] | .value[] | .hooks[].command' "$SETTINGS" \
    36	    | grep -oE '\.claude/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.sh' | sed -e 's#^\.claude/##' \
    37	    | sed -e 's#^hooks/#hook:#' -e 's#^scripts/#hook:scripts/#' | sort -u
    38	}
    39	enumerated_fence_ids() {
    40	  grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' "$FENCE" | grep -oE 'emit_block "[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"|pattern_id(: |=)"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"' \
    41	    | sed -E 's/.*"([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)"$/fence:\1/' | sort -u
    42	}
    43	enumerated_validator_ids() {
    44	  grep -oE '^[[:space:]]*# @guard validator:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+' "$VALIDATOR" | sed -E 's/.*validator:/validator:/' | sort -u
    45	}
    46	map_ids() { yq -r ".guards[] | select(.kind == \"$1\") | .id" "$MAP" | sort -u; }
    47	
    48	@test "GO-1 the origin map and floor.yaml parse with yq v4 and carry schema_version 1" {
    49	  run yq --version
    50	  [[ "$output" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]]
    51	  [ "$(yq '.schema_version' "$MAP")" = "1" ]
    52	  [ "$(yq '.schema_version' "$FLOOR")" = "1" ]
    53	  [ "$(yq '.guards | length' "$MAP")" -gt 0 ]
    54	}
    55	
    56	@test "GO-2 floor.yaml sha256 is pinned (update FLOOR_SHA256 deliberately when the floor changes)" {
    57	  source "$ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"

    59	  [ "$actual" = "$FLOOR_SHA256" ] || { echo "floor.yaml sha256 $actual != pinned $FLOOR_SHA256" >&2; false; }
    60	}
    61	
    62	@test "GO-3 every registered hook script has a row with a non-empty origin, and every hook row is registered" {
    63	  hooks="$(enumerated_hook_ids)"
    64	  [ "$(wc -l <<<"$hooks")" -ge 29 ]
    65	  while IFS= read -r id; do
    66	    ref="$(yq -r ".guards[] | select(.id == \"$id\") | .origin.ref // \"\"" "$MAP")"
    67	    [ -n "$ref" ] || { echo "hook $id has no row with an origin" >&2; false; }
    68	  done <<<"$hooks"

    71

    97	  done < <(yq -r '.guards[] | select(.kind == "gate" or .kind == "policy") | .script' "$MAP")
    98	}
    99	
   100	@test "GO-7 the floor: true rows are exactly floor.yaml floor_guards" {
   101	  diff <(yq -r '.floor_guards[]' "$FLOOR" | sort) <(yq -r '.guards[] | select(.floor == true) | .id' "$MAP" | sort)
   102	}
   103	
   104	@test "GO-8 enums hold, ids are unique and match the id pattern, origins are non-empty, dormant rows name an env var" {
   105	  [ -z "$(yq -r '.guards[].id' "$MAP" | sort | uniq -d)" ]
   106	  [ -z "$(yq -r '.guards[].id' "$MAP" | grep -vE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$' || true)" ]
   107	  [ "$(yq '[.guards[] | select((.kind | test("^(hook|fence|validator|gate|policy)$")) | not)] | length' "$MAP")" = "0" ]
   108	  [ "$(yq '[.guards[] | select((.class | test("^(harness|script|prose)$")) | not)] | length' "$MAP")" = "0" ]
   109	  [ "$(yq '[.guards[] | select((.status | test("^(active|dormant|telemetry)$")) | not)] | length' "$MAP")" = "0" ]
   110	  [ "$(yq '[.guards[] | select((.origin.kind | test("^(kf|issue|finding|cycle|design)$")) | not)] | length' "$MAP")" = "0" ]
   111	  [ "$(yq '[.guards[] | select((.origin.ref // "") == "")] | length' "$MAP")" = "0" ]
   112	  [ "$(yq '[.guards[] | select(.status == "dormant" and ((.knob | test("^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$")) | not))] | length' "$MAP")" = "0" ]
   113	  for g in team-role-guard team-role-guard-write team-skill-guard; do
   114	    [ "$(yq -r ".guards[] | select(.id == \"hook:safety/$g.sh\") | .status + \" \" + .knob" "$MAP")" = "dormant LOA_TEAM_MEMBER" ]
   115	  done
   116	  [ "$(yq -r '.guards[] | select(.id == "hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh") | .status + " " + .knob' "$MAP")" = "active implement_gate.mode" ]
   117	}
   118	
   119	@test "GO-9 guard-yield.sh validates the seeded map against the repository (exit 0, --check in sync)" {
   120	  run bash "$GY" --check

   125	@test "GO-10 a fixture settings.json with a command outside the canonical schema fails by name (exit 5)" {

   127	  run bash "$GY" --settings "$T/settings.json" "${OUTARGS[@]}"

   136	  run bash "$GY" --settings "$T/settings.json" "${OUTARGS[@]}"

   150	  run bash "$GY" --settings "$T/s3.json" "${OUTARGS[@]}"

index 00000000..cdf6f0ad
--- /dev/null
+++ b/evals/tests/arms-report.bats
@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/tests/arms-report.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.3)
+#
+# report.sh --arms over a fixture results tree (the layout run-arms.sh
+# writes): the pre-registered verdicts, the bootstrap interval, refuted share,
+# missed labels, the refusal while STATUS.json is not complete and the
+# --partial header. Thresholds come from the real review-recall suite.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  REPORT="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/report.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ar.XXXXXX")"
+  R="$T/arms"; S="$R/review-recall"; B="$S/b1"
+  mkdir -p "$B"
+  jq -n '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", batch:"b1", dry_run:false, source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457",
+          model_id:"claude-fable-5-1", arms:["baseline","no_companion","no_karpathy","no_rule_files"], fixtures:["pr-01","pr-02","pr-03"], trials:3}' \
+    > "$B/MANIFEST.json"
+  status_file complete
+}
+
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+status_file() {  # status_file <state>
+  jq -n --arg s "$1" '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", state:$s, batches:[{batch:"b1", state:$s}],
+                       source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457", model_id:"claude-fable-5-1"}' > "$S/STATUS.json"
+}
+
+# row <arm> <fixture> <trial> <recall> <missed-csv> [<cited> <refuted> <model> <source>]
+row() {
+  local arm="$1" fx="$2" t="$3" rc="$4" missed="$5" cited="${6:-4}" ref="${7:-1}"
+  local model="${8:-claude-fable-5-1}" src="${9:-864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457}"
+  mkdir -p "$B/$arm"
+  jq -cn --arg arm "$arm" --arg fx "$fx" --argjson t "$t" --argjson rc "$rc" --arg missed "$missed" \
+    --argjson cited "$cited" --argjson ref "$ref" --arg model "$model" --arg src "$src" \
+    '{status:"completed", arm:$arm, fixture:$fx, task_id:("review-" + $fx), trial:$t, model_id:$model, source_commit:$src,
+      executor:{model_id:$model, usage:{input_tokens:100, cache_read_input_tokens:900, output_tokens:0, cache_creation_input_tokens:0}},
+      graders:[{name:"recall-vs-defects.sh", details:{recall:$rc, planted:3,
+        detected:[], missed:($missed | split(",") | map(select(length > 0))),
+        findings_cited:$cited, findings_refuted:$ref}}]}' >> "$B/$arm/results.jsonl"
+}
+
+full_arm() {  # full_arm <arm> <recall> [<missed>] [<refuted>]
+  local fx t
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row "$1" "$fx" "$t" "$2" "${3:-}" 4 "${4:-1}"; done; done
+}
+
+@test "AR-1 complete run: equal recall reads no recall loss, a large drop reads recall loss, the informational arm says so" {
+  full_arm baseline 1
+  full_arm no_rule_files 1
+  full_arm no_karpathy 0.3333 "L2,L3" 1
+  full_arm no_companion 1
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md" --date 2026-10-14
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*no recall loss\*\*'
+  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*recall loss\*\*'
+  grep -E '^\| `no_companion` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q 'informational: yield only'
+  grep -E '^\| `baseline` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '(reference)'
+  # the interval of the drop and the missed labels are printed
+  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\[0.667, 0.667\]'
+  grep -q 'no_karpathy`: pr-01:L2 (3/3)' "$T/r.md"
+  grep -q '^# Control-arm report — 2026-10-14' "$T/r.md"
+  ! grep -q 'PARTIAL REPORT' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-2 a refuted-share rise beyond the threshold is a recall loss even with equal recall" {
+  full_arm baseline 1 "" 0
+  full_arm no_rule_files 1 "" 3
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*recall loss\*\*'
+  grep -q 'refuted share 0.750 > baseline 0.000' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-3 a missing trial or fixture is inconclusive; model or source skew is inconclusive" {
+  full_arm baseline 1
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_rule_files "$fx" "$t" 1 ""; done; done
+  row no_rule_files pr-03 1 1 ""
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_karpathy "$fx" "$t" 1 "" 4 1 claude-opus-5-5; done; done
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_companion "$fx" "$t" 1 "" 4 1 claude-fable-5-1 ffd25258; done; done
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
+  grep -q 'coverage: pr-03 1/3' "$T/r.md"
+  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
+  grep -q 'model skew' "$T/r.md"
+  grep -q 'source skew' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-4 a rule violation within the baseline's own trial-to-trial spread names no change (inconclusive)" {
+  # baseline trial means 1.0, 0.6, 1.0 (spread 0.4); the arm sits 0.2 lower on every fixture
+  local fx
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do row baseline "$fx" 1 1 ""; row baseline "$fx" 2 0.6 ""; row baseline "$fx" 3 1 ""; done
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do row no_rule_files "$fx" 1 0.8 ""; row no_rule_files "$fx" 2 0.4 ""; row no_rule_files "$fx" 3 0.8 ""; done
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
+  grep -q 'no change can be named' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-5 STATUS.json not complete: refused (exit 1); --partial writes, says so, and every verdict is inconclusive" {
+  full_arm baseline 1
+  full_arm no_rule_files 1
+  status_file running
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  grep -q "not 'complete'" <<<"$output"
+  [ ! -e "$T/r.md" ]
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md" --partial
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -q 'PARTIAL REPORT' "$T/r.md"
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
+  ! grep -q '\*\*no recall loss\*\*' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-7 a safeguard-refusal fallback to another model is skew: the arm is inconclusive and the fallback is named" {
+  full_arm baseline 1
+  full_arm no_rule_files 1
+  # one no_rule_files trial moved to Opus on a refusal (models_used + refusal_fallbacks, as execute-agent records them)
+  jq -c 'if .trial == 1 and .fixture == "pr-01" then .executor.models_used = {"claude-fable-5-1": 10, "global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5": 90}
+         | .executor.refusal_fallbacks = [{"from":"claude-fable-5-1","to":"global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5","category":"cyber"}] else . end' \
+    "$B/no_rule_files/results.jsonl" > "$B/x" && mv "$B/x" "$B/no_rule_files/results.jsonl"
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
+  grep -q 'model skew' "$T/r.md"
+  grep -q '1/9 trial(s) fell back to another model on a safeguard refusal' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-6 the default output path is evals/results/arms-report-<date>.md under the results root's repo; bad args exit 2" {
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite nope --results-dir "$R"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$T/missing" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --date 14-10-2026 --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+}

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

    return

  if [[ -n "$SUITE" ]]; then
    local suite_file="$SUITES_DIR/${SUITE}.yaml"
    if [[ ! -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: Suite not found: $suite_file" >&2
      exit 3
    fi

    # Read include patterns from suite
    local include_count
    include_count="$(yq -r '.tasks.include | length // 0' "$suite_file")"

    for i in $(seq 0 $((include_count - 1))); do
      local pattern
      pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.include[$i]" "$suite_file")"

      # Resolve glob pattern relative to evals/
      # Use bash globbing with globstar for ** patterns
      local had_globstar=false
      shopt -q globstar 2>/dev/null && had_globstar=true
      shopt -s globstar 2>/dev/null || true

      local glob_expanded=false
      for task_file in $EVALS_DIR/$pattern; do
        if [[ -f "$task_file" ]]; then
          TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          glob_expanded=true
        fi
      done

      # Restore globstar
      if [[ "$had_globstar" == "false" ]]; then
        shopt -u globstar 2>/dev/null || true
      fi

      # Fallback: if glob didn't match, try find in the directory
      if [[ "$glob_expanded" == "false" ]]; then
        # Extract directory portion from pattern
        local pattern_dir="${pattern%/*}"
        if [[ -d "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" ]]; then
          while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
            TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          done < <(find "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" \( -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' \) -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
        fi
      fi

          local exclude_pattern
          exclude_pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.exclude[$j]" "$suite_file")"
          if [[ "$(basename "$task_file")" == $exclude_pattern ]]; then
            excluded=true
            break

content.text:
Review written to `/workspace/review.md`. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED.

**What I checked.** I read the full diff across all 81 files and ran every test suite that is self-contained within `pr/head/` from a scratch copy (the `pr/` tree is untouched; an accidental `.git` and mode change I made there were reverted). The guard-yield, arm-toggles, arms-report, seed-corpus, sprint-kinds validator, cycle-ratio and grader suites all pass once their external dependencies are stubbed. I also cross-checked the origin map against the fence markers, validator markers, floor.yaml (sha pin matches) and the generated hooks table: all consistent.

**Findings, highest first:**

- **execute-agent.sh:266, blocking.** The `rule_files` toggle does not fail when the rule files are absent. I reproduced it: the `no_rule_files` arm exits 0 with evidence "removed: none present". That breaks the documented invariant that an arm never silently runs as its baseline, and this is one of the pre-registered arms whose verdict can license a deletion.
- **run-arms.sh:257.** Re-running a batch with the same source and model overwrites MANIFEST.json and resets the counters while results.jsonl keeps appending, so STATUS, MANIFEST and the report disagree.
- **guard-yield.sh:500.** A checkout under the temp prefix has every live block row classified as a replay.
- **seed-corpus-from-record.sh:736.** The redaction count in the dropped report double counts diff and base and never counts head.
- **implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:28.** App-zone permission widened from read to read-write with no mention in the PR and no test.

**Not flagged.** The prompt-budget workflow comment change is a correction, not a regression. The record-fixture task files reference fixture directories that are not in this diff, which I could not verify either way.
